properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 5:54PM MDT until October 11 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Kane County in southern Utah...
East Central Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 800 PM MDT.

* At 554 PM MDT, National Park Service officials reported
thunderstorms producing heavy rain and flash flooding across Zion
National Park. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...National Park Service reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, slot
canyons, and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Zion National Park, Springdale and Rockville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
As low clouds begin to clear late this evening and through the
overnight, conditions for fog development will become more
favorable, especially across eastern Indiana and western Ohio.
Some dense fog is possible and may result in visibility of one
quarter mile or less. Locations farther east into Ohio and farther
south into northern Kentucky could see visibility worsen through
daybreak.

Allow for greater distances between vehicles, use low beam
headlights, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Elko County; Southeastern Elko County; Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range; White Pine County; Southern Lander County and Southern Eureka County; Southwest Elko County; South Central Elko County; Northwestern Nye County; Northeastern Nye County
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 4:33PM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible.

* WHERE...Portions of eastern, northeast, and south central Nevada,
including the following areas, in eastern Nevada, White Pine. In
northeast Nevada, the Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in
Elko, South Central Elko and Southeastern Elko. In south central
Nevada, Northeastern Nye and Northwestern Nye.

* WHEN...Through 5 am PDT.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture from decaying Hurricane Rachel continues to move
northward, impacting portions of east-central and eastern Nevada
through roughly Monday. This significant moisture will interact
with upper level low pressure to bring widespread showers with
isolated thunderstorms to the watch area. Moderate to locally
heavy rain will cause excessive runoff and may result in rock,
mud, and debris flows in and near former fire burned areas, steep
terrain, and poorly drained urban areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH 5 AM PDT
